annotatedSteps.description: Equivalent resistance of 10 Ω and 15 Ω resistors in parallel
annotatedSteps.studentWork: 10 Ω and 15 Ω are in parallel: 1/R₁ = 1/10 + 1/15 = (3 + 2)/30 = 5/30 ⇒ R₁ = 6 Ω
annotatedSteps.teacherAnnotation: ✓ Correctly found equivalent resistance R₁ = 6 Ω

annotatedSteps.description: Equivalent resistance of 60 Ω and 40 Ω resistors and total circuit resistance
annotatedSteps.studentWork:
60 Ω and 40 Ω are in parallel: 1/R₂ = 1/60 + 1/40 = 2/100 ⇒ R₂ = 50 Ω
R₁ and R₂ are in series: R = 6 + 50 = 56 Ω

annotatedSteps.description: Calculation of total current drawn from the source
annotatedSteps.teacherAnnotation: ✓ Correct formula and substitution with error carried forward from (a)

annotatedSteps.description: Potential difference across the 10 Ω and 15 Ω combination
annotatedSteps.studentWork: Potential difference across the 10 Ω–15 Ω combination: V = I R₁ = 0.27 × 6 = 1.6 V
annotatedSteps.teacherAnnotation: ✓ Correct method and calculation using carried forward current

teacherNote: Marked against: Calculation of equivalent resistance of 10 Ω and 15 Ω parallel combination (R₁ = 6 Ω) (0.5); Calculation of equivalent resistance of 60 Ω and 40 Ω combination (R₂ = 24 Ω) and total circuit resistance (R = 30 Ω) (0.5); Calculation of total current drawn from the source using I = V/R (1); Calculation of potential difference across the 10 Ω and 15 Ω combination using V₁ = I R₁ (1). Your formulas and method across all three parts are completely sound. Be very careful with fraction addition when finding parallel resistance; finding the common denominator for 60 and 40 gives 24 Ω instead of 50 Ω.
